title: Setting Up a Company in Taiwan: Subsidiaries, Branches, Representative Offices, Procedures, and Work Permits
summary: Foreign companies and individuals may enter Taiwan through a subsidiary, branch, or representative office. Company setup does not grant a work permit or ARC.

title: Closing a Taiwan Company: What Happens to Capital and Company Assets?
summary: Paid-in capital becomes company property in a Taiwan company account. Closing, capital reduction, and suspension each follow different asset procedures.

title: Taiwan Traffic Accident Q&A: Scene Safety, Fault, Settlement, and Compensation
summary: After a Taiwan traffic accident, first secure the scene, report, and preserve evidence. Then review fault, claim deadlines, settlement, and compensation.

title: Entering the Taiwan Market: Key Differences Between a Subsidiary and a Branch
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary is a separate legal entity, but a branch is part of the foreign head office. Contracts, liability, tax, and profit remittance differ.

title: Taiwan Company Formation: Capital Remittance, Banking, and Foreign Hiring
summary: Company setup in Taiwan involves capital remittance, converting a preparatory bank account, and separate work-permit rules for hiring foreign managers.

title: Taiwan Massage: History and Legal Information
summary: Taiwan once limited massage work to people with visual impairments until a constitutional ruling. Report sexual harassment if it occurs during a massage.

title: Taiwan Divorce Q&A: Mediation, Litigation, Property, and Children
summary: A Taiwan divorce may use mutual consent, mediation, or litigation. Household registration, property division, and parental rights remain separate issues.

title: Taiwan Labor Law: Is Severance Pay Hard to Get in Taiwan?
summary: Taiwan pays severance on economic dismissal, not after voluntary resignation or most disciplinary dismissals. Amounts follow pension or labor-act service years.

title: Exceptions Where Employees Can Still Receive Severance After Voluntary Resignation
summary: Voluntary resignation in Taiwan usually yields no severance. Labor Standards Act Article 14 exceptions can still require payment, with a 30-day deadline.

title: Taiwan Gym Injury Claims: Case Study, Deadlines, Evidence, and Damages
summary: After a gym injury in Taiwan, consider litigation deadlines, evidence preservation, and damages. Gym liability insurance does not end a compensation dispute.

title: Entering Taiwan’s Cosmetics Market: Importer Selection, Product Registration, PIF Preparation and Retention, and Advertising Rules
summary: Foreign cosmetics brands entering Taiwan must choose an importer, complete product registration, and keep a PIF. Company setup alone does not complete them.

title: How Is Liability Assessed After an Overtaking Accident in Taiwan?
summary: Taiwan overtaking liability turns on Article 101, the location, and space to pass and return safely. This article reviews the rule and an anonymized case.

title: Taiwan Company Formation — Advanced Guide 1
summary: Taiwan company formation needs an investment-plan review, a registered office, and a bank account. A work permit and residence certificate come later.

title: Taiwan Minimum Service Period Clauses: Validity, Training Costs, and Contractual Penalties
summary: A Taiwan minimum service period clause is not automatically valid. It needs funded professional training or reasonable compensation, plus a statutory review.

title: Taiwan Company Formation — Advanced Guide 3: Finding a Business Location
summary: Company setup in Taipei requires checking whether the address may be used for the business. Restaurants often need a Business Location Prior Inquiry first.

title: Taiwan Inheritance and Parental Rights: A Guide for Surviving Families
summary: Taiwan inheritance, residual-property claims, and parental rights over a minor are separate processes after death. Cross-border families should not merge them.

title: Taiwan Logistics Businesses and Motor Freight Carrier Licensing: Formation, Acquisition, and Outsourcing
summary: A Taiwan logistics business is not always a licensed motor freight carrier. New formation, acquisition, and outsourcing follow different licensing rules.

title: Semiconductor Component Companies Entering Taiwan: How to Assess a Subsidiary, Branch, or Agent
summary: Semiconductor materials, components, and equipment firms should map Taiwan contracts, inventory, and staffing before choosing a subsidiary, branch, or agent.

title: Divorcing a Taiwanese spouse by agreement: what to check before signing
summary: Before signing a divorce agreement with a Taiwanese spouse, check terms, witnesses, registration and overseas documents, plus any separate child arrangements.

title: Living abroad while your Taiwanese spouse is in Taiwan: preparing for a divorce consultation
summary: Prepare for a Taiwan divorce consultation from abroad: organize consent, address details, existing proceedings and documents, then check service and attendance.

title: Divorce from a Taiwanese spouse: planning your child’s life across two countries
summary: Plan a child’s life across two countries after divorce from a Taiwanese spouse: check authority and orders, then prepare care, contact and child expense plans.

title: Marrying a Taiwanese National: A U.S. Citizen's Registration Checklist
summary: Planning a U.S.–Taiwan marriage? Plan where to marry, document verification, household registration and spouse visas before booking travel and appointments.

title: A Baby in a U.S.–Taiwan Family: Citizenship, Birth Records and Taiwan Household Registration
summary: Expecting a baby in a U.S.–Taiwan family? Separate citizenship, birth records, Taiwan household registration and passports, with official guidance at each step.

title: Taiwan Income Tax Residence When You Arrive or Leave Midyear
summary: A move in or out of Taiwan can change what income you report. Check domicile, the tax-year day count, where you worked, who paid you, and departure date.

title: When Someone Who Lived Abroad Dies Holding Assets in Taiwan
summary: If a non-ROC national who lived abroad dies owning Taiwan property, estate tax reaches only property situated in Taiwan, with the return due within six months.

title: Inheriting Taiwan Property as a Foreigner: Which Law Applies and How Land Is Registered
summary: Foreign heirs to a Taiwan estate must check which country’s succession law applies, limits on foreigners holding land, and why estate tax clearance comes first.

title: The Taiwan Employment Gold Card, Filed by the Applicant
summary: The Employment Gold Card is filed by you, not an employer: one card combining a work permit, resident visa, ARC and re-entry permit for one to three years.

title: Residence in Taiwan as the Foreign Spouse of a Taiwanese National: From ARC to Divorce or Bereavement
summary: A foreign spouse of a household-registered Taiwanese can get a resident visa and ARC, extend it, and may stay after the spouse dies or after a divorce.

title: When Can You Apply for Permanent Residence (APRC) in Taiwan? General, Spouse and Professional Routes
summary: Compare Taiwan APRC routes under the Immigration Act and Foreign Professionals Act: how residence years count, the conduct test, and what can cost you the card.

title: Enforcing a Foreign Judgment Against Assets in Taiwan
summary: A foreign judgment does not go straight to Taiwan's enforcement court. Check recognition rules, get an enforcement judgment, and prove finality and service.

title: Instructing a Taiwan Lawyer From Outside Taiwan
summary: To hire a Taiwan lawyer from abroad, confirm they may practice, agree the fee basis, and put the appointment, service agent and foreign papers in valid form.

title: Exit ban in Taiwan: what a foreigner should do at the airport
summary: Stopped at a Taiwan airport? An exit ban can come from a prosecutor, court, tax bureau or enforcement office. Learn who imposed it and what a lawyer needs.

title: Summoned by Taiwan police or prosecutors as a foreigner: rights, the first 24 hours and bail
summary: Got a police notice or prosecutor's summons in Taiwan? Learn your right to silence and counsel, interpreter rules, the 24-hour arrest limit, bail and visa risk.

title: Told your Taiwan job is ending? What foreign professionals should check in the first week
summary: Told your Taiwan job is ending? Check the legal ground, notice pay, severance and any resignation paper first, then what it means for your permit or Gold Card.

title: When a Taiwan Crypto Platform Blocks Your Withdrawal
summary: A frozen withdrawal or closed account calls for records of what the platform owes and a check of its Taiwan registration. Civil and criminal routes differ.

title: Buying and Selling a Flat in Taiwan as a Foreigner
summary: A foreign buyer of a flat in Taiwan needs a Land Act reciprocity check and pays deed tax. On sale, tax residence sets the house-and-land income-tax rates.

title: Taiwan Shares, US Investors and Two Tax Systems
summary: Holding Taiwan-listed shares and ETFs directly can bring Taiwan transaction tax and dividend withholding, plus separate US tax and reporting. Fund type matters.

title: The paperwork after a crash in Taiwan
summary: Police records after a crash in Taiwan can be requested in stages. Using the national portal and appointing someone to act for you each come with conditions.

title: Left-turning cars and oncoming scooters: how Taiwan courts split fault
summary: In Taiwan, a left-turning driver must yield to an oncoming scooter. Courts in three civil cases assigned 70%, 60% and 50% fault after examining the evidence.

title: Taiwan's Commercial Court now reaches more private-company disputes
summary: From 1 Oct 2026 Taiwan's Commercial Court uses lower NT$ thresholds for some private-company shareholder disputes; the claim type still decides the forum.

title: A foreign brand's Taiwan store: company, branch, or master franchise
summary: Foreign brands entering Taiwan choose a company, branch, or master franchise. Investment filings, trademark licenses, and Fair Trade franchise rules differ.

title: Taiwan wage disputes: mediation and a union strike vote
summary: Taiwan wage disputes separate mediation from a lawful strike vote. Foreign employers should track Labor Act deadlines, union ballots, and settlement records.

title: Closing a Taiwan subsidiary or branch: when can the remaining cash leave?
summary: Dissolution registration starts Taiwan liquidation; it does not clear tax, labor, or creditor claims. Foreign parents need a checklist before remitting capital.

title: Injured at a Taiwan hospital: the chart, mediation, and a lawsuit
summary: Foreign patients hurt in Taiwan can request medical records, try mediation, then sue. Limitation periods and chart language often differ from home practice.

title: When a Taiwan company must recognize its overseas subsidiary's profits
summary: Taiwan's corporate CFC rules can pull low-tax overseas subsidiary income into the parent tax base when control tests are met. Exemptions need early documents.

title: A purchase dispute in Taiwan: where can a foreign buyer complain?
summary: Foreign buyers disputing a Taiwan online order should keep payment proof, complain to the seller, then use consumer-protection or small-claims paths in Taiwan.

title: A Taiwan fraud loss: the damages claim inside the criminal case
summary: Victims of Taiwan fraud may file an ancillary civil claim inside the criminal case under the Code of Criminal Procedure, changing timing versus a separate suit.

title: Gift tax when a foreigner gives Taiwan property
summary: Foreigners owe Taiwan gift tax only on Taiwan property. The NT$2.44 million yearly exemption counts once per donor; filing is due 30 days after it is exceeded.

title: When a Taiwan bank account is listed as a warning account
summary: When police or prosecutors flag a Taiwan bank account as a warning account, the bank freezes it. How holders object and how victims reclaim remaining funds.

title: Getting a Taiwan residential deposit back as a foreign tenant
summary: Taiwan caps most residential deposits at two months' rent, refundable less lease debts at move-out. When landlords may reclaim housing and how mediation works.

title: Declaring Taiwan FX conversions and remittances from NT$500,000 up
summary: Taiwan FX conversions of NT$500,000 or more are declared through a bank. When the form suffices, when papers are checked, when Central Bank approval applies.

title: Taiwan company responsible persons: duties to the company and joint liability to others
summary: Under Company Act Article 23, responsible persons owe a Taiwan company loyalty and care, and share liability for harm from their unlawful acts in its business.

title: Child support across borders: enforcing in Taiwan and bringing in foreign orders
summary: How Taiwan enforces child support under the Family Act, how foreign orders are screened by Taiwan courts, and why Taiwan orders reach only Taiwan assets.

title: Labor dispute mediation in Taiwan for foreign employees
summary: Foreign employees in Taiwan can take wage and dismissal disputes to labor bureau mediation. How it relates to court mediation and residence during a dispute.

title: Inheriting a Taiwan Bank Account From the U.S.: What to Check Before Signing a Power of Attorney
summary: Before signing a power of attorney in the U.S., confirm the Taiwan bank’s inheritance requirements, the agent’s powers, and the document-authentication route.

title: When the other parent keeps your child in Taiwan: what a Taiwan family court can do
summary: Taiwan is not a Hague Abduction Convention party. How its family courts decide custody, when they order a child moved, and how they treat U.S. custody orders.

title: Four cut-ins and three brake checks near Linkou, and a taxi that wouldn't yield either
summary: A truck driver cut into a taxi's lane four times and braked three times near Linkou. Taiwan's High Court cut his sentence: the taxi had fought for the lane too.

title: Getting a US divorce decree onto Taiwan's household register
summary: A final US divorce decree does not change Taiwan's household register by itself. How registration works, what Article 402 asks, and when a Taiwan court decides.

title: How a traffic quarrel in Keelung became a bat attack and an NT$2.08 million award
summary: A Keelung traffic quarrel ended in a baseball-bat assault. Courts imposed seven months for injury and awarded the victim NT$2.08 million in civil damages.

title: Micron’s Taiwan Dispute: Trade Secrets, Employees and Proof
summary: Micron’s DRAM dispute had different outcomes for UMC, Fujian Jinhua and individuals. Taiwan’s record shows why access controls and proof of prevention matter.

title: TSMC Arizona: What the U.S. Award and Taiwan Approval Actually Cover
summary: TSMC Arizona's CHIPS award, Taiwan investment approval and technology rules have different scopes, with distinct implications for U.S. suppliers and partners.

title: Honked at from behind, a driver reversed into the other car three times and called it self-defence
summary: Honked at on a New Taipei expressway, a driver reversed into the car behind three times. Courts rejected self-defence: five months for endangering road traffic.

title: Taiwan’s Export Entity List and the U.S. EAR: Two License Questions for One Shipment
summary: Since June 2025, exports from Taiwan to Huawei, SMIC and other listed entities need Taiwan permits. The permits do not resolve U.S. EAR licensing requirements.

title: A Taiwanese Supplier's New Bank Account: Who Approved It?
summary: A changed bank account in a familiar email thread can leave a Taiwan supplier's invoice disputed. How to verify authority and preserve evidence after payment.

title: An ‘Immigration Officer’ Calls About Your Taiwan ARC
summary: A call about your Taiwan ARC may need a prompt response. Verify the office, document request and payment channel through NIA contacts you find independently.

title: A Parcel-Pickup Job in Taiwan: Whose Package Are You Collecting?
summary: A paid parcel-pickup job can involve other people's bank cards. Job instructions, messages and delivery records can help establish what you knew and did.

title: Trade Secret Litigation in Taiwan: Injunctions, Evidence and Damages
summary: U.S. chip firms can seek civil relief in Taiwan without a criminal conviction. Interim orders, evidence preservation and confidentiality need distinct showings.

title: Repair Visits to Your Taiwan Rental While You Are Away
summary: Covered residential lease terms in Taiwan require reasonable advance notice for necessary repair visits. Tenants may not refuse without a proper reason.

title: Asking a Taiwan Business for a Copy of Your Personal Data
summary: A Taiwan business must decide on a personal data access or copy request within 15 days. An extension needs written reasons; necessary costs may be charged.

title: Who started it did not matter to a Taiwan court after a driver blocked the same car twice and got out with a bat
summary: A driver in Taiwan blocked a car twice and approached with a wooden baseball bat. The court imposed three months in prison for coercion, convertible to a fine.

title: A driver stopped in Route 66's fast lane to confront the motorist behind
summary: A driver forced the car behind to stop on Taoyuan's Route 66 at night. The court imposed three months in prison, convertible to a fine at NT$1,000 per day.

title: The freeway chase was on his own dashcam too
summary: A freeway chase ended in a collision. The Supreme Court dismissed a driver's appeal after he failed to identify a legal error, leaving his conviction intact.

title: A Taiwan protection order when you are a foreign spouse
summary: Foreign spouses can seek protection in Taiwan without filing for divorce. Learn who applies, what orders can cover, and how custody and ARC issues differ.

title: The 52 seconds a Taiwan court subtracted from a road-rage case
summary: A driver chased a scooter, blocked it twice and swore at its rider in Zhonghe. The High Court upheld the acquittal on coercion and public insult charges.

title: A two-second stop in Taipei was not enough to prove dangerous driving
summary: A car and a motorcycle stopped in separate Taipei incidents. Courts cancelled the driver's penalties but upheld the rider's after reviewing dashcam footage.

title: U.S.–Taiwan Chip Investment: Royalties, Fees and the Treaty Gap
summary: U.S. chip suppliers face Taiwan withholding on royalties and service fees while tax relief bills remain pending. Contract terms shape the cost of expansion.

title: Taiwan marital property division with an American spouse
summary: How Taiwan divides marital property when one spouse is American: which law applies, how US accounts and a 401k fit, the short deadlines, and freezing assets.

title: On Call at the Fab: Taiwan Working-Hour Rules for a U.S. Vendor's Field Engineers
summary: Field engineers a U.S. equipment vendor employs in Taiwan work under the Labor Standards Act: eight-hour days, 46 overtime hours a month, no exempt category.

title: Who Paid the Recruiter? Taiwan's Migrant-Worker Fee Rules and the U.S. Chip Supply Chain
summary: Taiwan caps what brokers may charge migrant workers. A U.S. trade deal, signed but not yet in force, would bar worker-paid recruitment fees in manufacturing.

title: Taiwan Property Still in a Late Parent's Name: What Happens If the Heirs Do Not Register
summary: Taiwan gives heirs six months to register inherited land. A fine may follow, then notice and listed management after a year, and a public tender 15 years later.

title: Taiwan Estate Tax in 2026: The Figures, and Who Pays on Gifts Made Before Death
summary: How Taiwan taxes the estate of a resident who dies in 2026: the NT$13.33 million exemption, deductions and rates, plus the new rule on gifts before death.

title: Dying Without a Will in Taiwan: Who Inherits, in What Order, and How Much
summary: With no will in Taiwan, the spouse inherits with one rank of relatives, and that rank sets the spouse's share. Renunciation does not trigger representation.

title: Renouncing a Taiwanese Parent's Debts From Japan: The Three-Month Deadline
summary: A child in Japan can renounce a Taiwanese parent's debts only in a Taiwan court, within three months. Document authentication in Japan does not stop that clock.

title: Does a U.S. Will or Living Trust Reach a Taipei Apartment and a Taiwan Bank Account?
summary: A U.S. will and revocable living trust do not, on their own, transfer a Taipei apartment or a Taiwan bank deposit. Taiwan law tests each document separately.

title: When Scam Money Lands in a Taiwan Account and You Are Overseas
summary: A victim abroad can file a criminal complaint in Taiwan via an agent. What Taiwan police and banks can hold or return from the account, and what they cannot.

title: When a Korean National Dies in Taiwan: Korean Law Picks the Heirs, Taiwan Taxes the Local Estate
summary: When a Korean national living in Taiwan dies there, Korean law generally decides the heirs, while Taiwan taxes only Taiwan assets and limits the deductions.

title: Stalked in Taiwan: the police warning, the court order, and a six-month deadline
summary: For stalking tied to sex or gender, Taiwan police can issue a written warning, a court can make a protection order, and a complaint is due within six months.

title: Owed NT$100,000 or Less in Taiwan: Small Claims Costs, Mediation, and Appeals
summary: Taiwan sends money claims of NT$100,000 or less to a small-claims track with a NT$1,500 court fee, court mediation first, and appeals on points of law only.

title: A Sexual Harassment Complaint in a Taiwan Workplace: The Employer's Duties and the Employee's Options
summary: Taiwan employers must act at once on a sexual harassment complaint, notify the local authority and close the case in two months. Staff may go there directly.

title: Maternity and Parental Leave in Taiwan as a Foreign Employee: What Is Paid in 2026, and by Whom
summary: Foreign employees in Taiwan can take maternity and unpaid parental leave. Employment Insurance pays the parental allowance but covers only some foreigners.

title: Taiwan Apartment Management Committees: Unpaid Fees, Leaks, Rules and Short-Term Lets
summary: Taiwan's Condominium Administration Act decides who pays for shared parts, how a management committee collects unpaid fees, and how building rules bind tenants.

title: Who Owns Code and Designs Made in Taiwan by Employees and Freelancers?
summary: Under Taiwan's Copyright Act an employee is the author of work made on the job, and a paid freelancer keeps the copyright unless the contract says otherwise.

title: Selling Apps, Games or SaaS to Taiwan Without an Office: When VAT Registration Applies
summary: A foreign company with no Taiwan office must register for business tax once e-service sales to individuals in Taiwan pass NT$600,000 a year, up from NT$480,000.

title: Naturalizing in Taiwan: The One-Year Renunciation Deadline and the High-Level Professional Exception
summary: Taiwan gives most naturalized foreigners one year to prove loss of their original nationality. High-level professionals are exempt from that requirement.

title: A Taiwan DUI Can Reach Beyond the Driver’s Seat
summary: A Taiwan drunk-driving stop can fine a sober passenger, impound the car, suspend or revoke the license, and restrict a foreign resident's exit or stay.

title: Taken to a Taiwan Police Station: The First 24 Hours Are Not a Release Promise
summary: After an arrest in Taiwan, 24 hours is the prosecutor's deadline to seek court detention, not a release time. Interpreter waits, bail and exit bans explained.

title: Buying a Home in Taiwan: Reciprocity, Presale Contracts and Resale Tax
summary: Taiwan lists Korea and Japan as fully reciprocal and U.S. buyers by state. Presale contracts cannot be freely assigned; nonresidents pay 45% or 35% on gains.

title: House Title, Residual-Property Distribution, Damages, and Post-Divorce Support in a Taiwan Divorce
summary: House title, residual-property distribution, damages, and post-divorce support are separate claims with different elements, calculations, and time limits.

title: A Taiwan Subsidiary's Tax Year: May Return, September Prepayment, 5% Surtax
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary files its 20% income tax return in May, prepays half of last year's tax in September, and may owe 5% on retained earnings and a minimum tax.

title: Taiwan Subsidiary Dividends to a US Parent: Why 21% Still Applies
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary withholds 21 percent on dividends to a foreign parent. Japan and Korea cap it at 10 percent, Vietnam at 15, and no US agreement is in force.

title: Paying a US or Vietnamese Parent from Taiwan: Withholding on Royalties, Service Fees and Interest
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary paying royalties, loan interest or Taiwan-source service fees to a parent with no Taiwan office withholds 20% unless an agreement applies.

title: Taiwan Transfer Pricing Documentation: Local File, Master File and CbCR Thresholds
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary or branch with related-party deals must have transfer pricing documents ready at filing and produce them within a month of a request.

title: CPA Audits, CPA-Certified Tax Returns and Bookkeeping Rules for Taiwan Subsidiaries and Branches
summary: Taiwan companies need CPA-audited accounts from NT$30 million paid-in capital, or below it at NT$100 million revenue or 100 insured staff; tax has its own test.

title: Vietnamese Companies with Taiwan Income: What the Taiwan–Vietnam Tax Agreement Changes
summary: Taiwan withholds 21% on dividends, 20% on royalties and most interest paid abroad. A 1998 agreement caps them at 15%, 15%, 10% for Vietnamese beneficial owners.

title: Business Tax for a New Taiwan Subsidiary: 5% VAT, Bimonthly Returns, Zero-Rated Exports and E-Invoices
summary: As of October 2026 a Taiwan subsidiary pays 5% business tax on output minus input tax, files every two months by the 15th and must upload e-invoices on time.

title: Taiwan Payroll for US Assignees and Foreign Hires: Withholding and Social Insurance
summary: Work done in Taiwan is usually taxed there even if a US parent pays. Non-residents face 18 percent withholding, or 6 percent up to NT$44,250 a month in 2026.

title: Running a Taiwan Branch: Deducting Head-Office Overhead and Sending Profits Home
summary: A Taiwan branch may deduct a revenue-based share of head-office overhead if two tests are met and it files a CPA-certified report. Remittances are not withheld.

title: Taiwan R&D and Equipment Tax Credits for Foreign-Owned Subsidiaries: 15%, 5%, 25% and a 30% Cap
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary can credit 15% of R&D spending or 5% of smart machinery and AI investment against corporate tax, capped at 30% of each year's tax, to 2029.

title: Taiwan Representative Offices: What They May Do and What They Still File
summary: A Taiwan representative office may sign, quote, bid and buy for its parent but may not sell. A buying-only office owes no VAT or income tax but must withhold.

title: Disputing a Taiwan Tax Assessment: 30 Days to Seek Re-examination, Then Appeal and Court
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary that disputes a tax assessment must apply for re-examination within 30 days, then may appeal to the Ministry of Finance and the courts.

title: Selling Shares in a Taiwan Subsidiary: The 0.3% Transaction Tax and When the Gain Is Taxed
summary: A foreign parent selling Taiwan subsidiary shares pays 0.3% transaction tax; the gain is taxed only if the stake is not a security or the firm is property-rich.

title: Closing a Taiwan Subsidiary or Branch: The 45-Day, 15-Day and 30-Day Tax Filings
summary: Closing a Taiwan subsidiary means a final-period return within 45 days, VAT deregistration within 15 days and a liquidation return within 30 days of completion.

title: Taiwan Stamp Tax for Foreign-Owned Subsidiaries: Contracts, Receipts and Where You Sign
summary: As of October 2026, Taiwan stamp tax is 0.4% on receipts, 0.1% on work contracts and NT$12 per goods sale contract, even between parent and subsidiary.

title: Taxed Twice on One Profit: Taiwan's Mutual Agreement Procedure, and What US Groups Use Instead
summary: Taiwan's tax agreements with Japan, Korea and Vietnam allow a mutual agreement request within three years of the first notice. US groups use domestic remedies.

title: Enforcing a US Arbitral Award in Taiwan: The Recognition Ruling, Required Documents and Reciprocity
summary: Taiwan is not a New York Convention state, but its Arbitration Act lets a court recognize a US award by ruling, after which it is enforceable like a judgment.

title: Hiring in Taiwan Without a Local Entity: Employer of Record, Permanent Establishment and Work Permits
summary: A US company can put staff in Taiwan without a subsidiary, but Taiwan labor law follows the worker, work permits need a Taiwanese employer, and PE risk is real.

title: Terminating a Taiwan Distributor: Notice Periods, Compensation Claims, Inventory and Customer Data
summary: Taiwan has no dealer-protection statute. Whether you owe notice or compensation turns on the Civil Code's commercial-agent rules and on what your contract says.

title: Unpaid Invoices From a Taiwan Buyer: Payment Orders, Provisional Attachment, Lawsuits and the Two-Year Limit
summary: A US seller can collect from a Taiwanese buyer with an NT$500 court payment order, but if Taiwan law governs, claims for the price of goods expire in two years.

title: Cannabis, THC and CBD in Taiwan: possession, transport and medicine imports
summary: Taiwan treats cannabis possession, use and transport differently. CBD medicines and other products have separate rules; US legality does not authorize import.

title: Installing Equipment at a Taiwan Fab: Tax on the Tool, the Installation Fee and a Six-Month Project
summary: A head office's direct equipment sale to a Taiwan buyer is ordinary trade; on-site installation fees are Taiwan-source, withheld at 20% or 3% under Article 25.

title: Funding a Taiwan Subsidiary with Parent Loans: The 3:1 Limit on Interest Deductions
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary loses part of its interest deduction once related-party debt exceeds three times equity; interest paid to a US parent bears 20% withholding.

title: Equity Awards from a US Parent: Taiwan Taxes Options at Exercise and Has No RSU Ruling
summary: Taiwan taxes a foreign parent's stock options in the exercise year, prorated by days in Taiwan, and the subsidiary files in January. We found no RSU ruling.

title: When a Taiwan Subsidiary Owes Tax: Exit Bans on Its Chairman and Criminal Liability
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary with NT$2 million of final tax and fines unpaid can see its chairman barred from leaving; below NT$20 million of final debt, more is needed.

title: Pillar Two and a Taiwan Subsidiary: The Parent Runs the 15% Test
summary: Official Taiwan texts show no Pillar Two top-up tax as of October 2026, yet a Vietnamese parent tests Taiwan profits at 15%; US groups can elect a safe harbour.

title: Shipping Goods to Taiwan: Import Duty, 5% Business Tax, Commodity Tax and a 0.04% Fee
summary: Taiwan Customs collects import duty, 5% business tax, commodity tax on seven product groups and a 0.04% trade fee; general-method importers credit the 5% tax.

title: Taiwan Customs Value for Related-Party Imports: Price Tests, Year-End True-Ups and Advance Rulings
summary: A related-party link alone does not let Taiwan Customs reject an import price, and its year-end transfer pricing scheme covers only entries flagged at import.

title: Taiwan as a Regional Hub: Free Trade Zones, Bonded Warehouses, Science Parks and the FTZ Income Tax Exemption
summary: Goods re-exported through a Taiwan free trade zone, bonded warehouse or logistics center bear no duty or VAT, while the FTZ income tax exemption needs approval.

title: Taiwan Income Tax on Cross-Border E-Services: 20% Withholding or a May Return
summary: Foreign sellers of online games, ads and other real-time e-services owe Taiwan income tax: Taiwan business buyers withhold 20%, consumer sales are filed in May.

title: Vietnamese Tax Incentives and Taiwan's CFC Rules: A Low-Tax Test Decided Case by Case
summary: As of October 2026, Vietnam's standard 20% rate is above Taiwan's 14% CFC line and its 10% incentive rate below it; Taiwan judges such regimes case by case.

title: Called as a witness in a Taiwan criminal case
summary: Taiwan witness summons: attendance, refusal to testify, cross-examination limits and interpreters. Check the issuing authority and a request to change the date.

title: Settling a Taiwan criminal complaint before the money arrives
summary: Withdrawing a Taiwan criminal complaint before payment can leave it withdrawn even if money never arrives. Check offense, deadline and effect on accomplices.

title: Taiwan declined to prosecute: the complainant’s ten-day reconsideration period
summary: Taiwan non-prosecution review has a ten-day period. Check valid service, filing arrival, complainant status and a separate court application requiring a lawyer.

title: Getting a seized phone back in Taiwan before the criminal case ends
summary: A seized phone in Taiwan may be returned before a case ends. Learn the retention test, temporary return and court review of a prosecutor’s seizure disposition.

title: An assault in Taiwan: injury evidence, self-defense and compensation
summary: After assault in Taiwan, medical records, video and a clear complaint serve different purposes. Ordinary injury has a six-month complaint clock with exceptions.

title: A Taiwan criminal judgment arrived: when the appeal period starts
summary: A Taiwan criminal judgment can start a 20-day appeal period when served. The filing route depends on whether it is an ordinary judgment or a summary judgment.

title: Deferred prosecution in Taiwan still carries deadlines
summary: Deferred prosecution in Taiwan can require payment, treatment or service. Its period starts when final, and missed duties can reopen the investigation or case.

title: Visiting a family member held in a Taiwan detention center
summary: Family visits to a Taiwan detention center depend on contact restrictions and facility rules. Lawyer meetings, remote contact and identifying documents differ.

title: What a Taiwan police criminal-record certificate leaves out
summary: A Taiwan police certificate can omit specified convictions without erasing the case. The sentence type, completion date and later record affect what it shows.

title: Reporting sexual assault in Taiwan as an English-speaking adult
summary: An adult sexual-assault victim in Taiwan can seek care and reporting support. Consent, a support person, protected proceedings and complaint exceptions matter.

title: Shoplifting and keeping found property in Taiwan
summary: Taiwan treats theft and keeping lost property as distinct crimes. Returning an item may matter, but store theft does not end when the store forgives it.

title: A short Taiwan prison sentence: payment, service or suspension
summary: A short Taiwan prison sentence may allow fine conversion or community service, subject to approval. A suspended sentence has separate conditions and deadlines.

title: Prepaying a Taiwan packaging supplier: what happens if the slot slips?
summary: A Taiwan packaging prepayment may reserve a production slot without fixing a delivery date. The contract should explain what happens to the money if work slips.

title: Buying a Taiwan AI-Chip Startup: Investor Status and the Closing Date
summary: US buyers of private Taiwan AI-chip companies should check investor ownership, control rights, investment approval and merger filing before committing to close.

title: A Singapore Arbitration Clause for a Taiwan Supply Contract
summary: For Singapore buyers of Taiwan goods: connect the arbitration clause to the contracting supplier, its assets and the Taiwan enforcement process before signing.

title: Funding a New Taiwan Subsidiary: Singapore Company Records and Capital Remittance
summary: For Singapore holding companies: prepare ownership records for a new Taiwan subsidiary and align capital remittance with the approved investment plan.

title: Selling Singapore Goods to Taiwan: Before You Quote an ASTEP Price
summary: Singapore exporters selling to Taiwan should verify ASTEP origin, arrange supporting records and agree who bears the cost if tariff preference is refused.

title: Getting Molds and Test Fixtures Back From a Taiwan Supplier
summary: For US buyers moving production from Taiwan: establish who owns the molds, assess the supplier's right to retain them and agree on a workable physical handover.

title: When a Taiwan Shipment Fails Inspection
summary: US buyers finding defects in Taiwan shipments need prompt notice and preserved samples. Repair talks do not by themselves stop the deadlines for legal remedies.

title: Your Taiwan Investment Closed. Now the Company Won't Share Its Records.
summary: US investors denied Taiwan company records should check company type, shareholder status and reporting rights before choosing how to pursue missing documents.

title: Buying a Taiwan Business: Who Employs the Engineers After Closing?
summary: US buyers of a Taiwan business need to distinguish a share purchase from a change of employer when planning employee notices and recognition of prior service.

title: The Shipment Arrived. The Taiwan Customer Still Has Not Paid.
summary: Where Taiwan law applies, a merchant's claim for the price of goods lapses in two years. A demand letter stops the clock only if suit follows within six months.

title: Ten Days After a Taiwan Prosecutor Declines to Charge: Reconsideration, Then a Court Motion
summary: After a Taiwan prosecutor declines to charge, a complainant has 10 days to seek reconsideration and, if refused, 10 more to ask a court for leave to prosecute.

title: Deferred Prosecution in Taiwan: The Conditions, and What a Complainant Can Do
summary: A Taiwan prosecutor can defer prosecution on conditions such as paying the victim. The complainant may seek reconsideration or ask to revoke the deferral.

title: A Taiwan Summons Arrives: What Ignoring It Means for a Defendant and for a Witness
summary: Skip a lawful Taiwan summons without good reason and a defendant may be brought in by warrant; a witness may also be fined up to NT$30,000 as of October 2026.

title: Taiwan Injury Settlement: Who Can Withdraw the Complaint, and Until When?
summary: Taiwan prosecutes injury under Article 277, paragraph 1 and negligent injury only on complaint. Withdrawal is open until oral argument closes at first instance.

title: Appealing a Taiwan Criminal Judgment: Twenty Days, and the Cases That End at the Second Instance
summary: A Taiwan criminal appeal is due 20 days after service. Under Article 376, listed offenses such as theft end at the second instance, with one exception.

title: After a Taiwan Criminal Sentence Becomes Final: Fine Conversion, Probation, and Removal of Foreigners
summary: A Taiwan prison term of six months or less may be converted at NT$1,000, 2,000 or 3,000 a day. Probation runs two to five years. A foreigner may be deported.

title: When a Taiwan Chip Supplier Blames Its Testing Lab
summary: A Taiwan chip supplier may be responsible for an outside testing lab's mistakes. Contract terms, the promised tests and proof of loss shape the buyer's claim.

title: Signing for a Taiwan Company Before It Exists
summary: Taiwan company name approval does not complete incorporation. Article 19 addresses contracts made in an unregistered company's name and personal liability.

title: Changing Bookkeepers in Taiwan: The Records Your Company Still Needs
summary: Changing Taiwan bookkeepers does not end record-retention duties. Paper disposal needs more than a scan, and electronic records must remain fully readable.

title: Preserving Evidence Before a Civil Suit in Taiwan
summary: Taiwan allows evidence-preservation motions before suit. The legal ground, evidence location, facts to be proved and notice to other parties shape the request.

title: When a Taiwan Employee Is a Suspect, Who Is Company-Paid Counsel Defending?
summary: Company-paid Taiwan criminal defense raises questions about the client, consent, confidentiality and conflicts. Employees retain rights during questioning.

title: A Delaware LLC Investing in Taiwan: Identity, Ownership and Signing Authority
summary: A Delaware LLC investing in a Taiwan company needs records linking its legal identity, ownership and signing authority to the investor named in the application.

title: A US Company's Request for an Opponent's Documents in Taiwan Civil Litigation
summary: A US company seeking an opponent's records in Taiwan civil litigation must identify the documents, facts to prove and the basis for requiring their production.

title: A US Citizen Arrested in Taiwan: AIT Contact and Local Defense
summary: US citizens arrested in Taiwan can ask authorities to notify AIT. Consular assistance, Taiwan defense counsel and interpreting have distinct roles in the case.

title: Form 5471 Preparation: Records to Request From a Taiwan Company
summary: After a Form 5471 filing duty is confirmed, a Taiwan company's records can support US preparation through clear periods, currencies and accounting adjustments.

title: Taiwan Sick Leave: Half Wages and 2026 Protection Against Adverse Action for Up to Ten Days
summary: Ordinary sick leave carries half pay for up to 30 days a year. Employers pay half without labor-insurance benefits, or top up a lower benefit to that level.

title: Leaving a One-Year Taiwan Lease Before the Term Ends
summary: If your Taiwan lease permits early exit at will, give at least one month's notice. The penalty for ending without that notice is capped at one month's rent.

title: Taiwan's 16% Cap on Private Loan Interest
summary: Taiwan private-loan interest over 16% a year is void only for the excess. Lending alone creates no interest. No due date: set a month or more and demand return.

title: Unpaid wages when a Taiwan employer closes, liquidates, or goes bankrupt
summary: After closure, liquidation, or adjudicated bankruptcy, wages under six months share first-mortgage rank. An advance needs contributions and an unpaid demand.

title: Part-time work for foreign students in Taiwan: the permit and the 20-hour week
summary: A foreign student in Taiwan applies for the work permit. Outside winter and summer breaks the cap is 20 hours a week, and the permit lasts at most one year.

title: False Financial Reports in Taiwan: Who May Claim Civil Damages
summary: Taiwan's false-report claims can cover good-faith buyers, sellers, and holders who suffer resulting loss. A price fall alone does not establish the whole claim.

title: Who Must Return Money Mistakenly Sent to a Taiwan Account
summary: Taiwan law may require return of a mistaken transfer. Four payment categories limit recovery; knowledge and the remaining benefit affect the recipient's duty.

title: Who Approves the Accounts When a Taiwan Company Has One Shareholder
summary: Taiwan companies need yearly accounts approval, even with one foreign parent. Company type determines who approves, and directors may serve past their term end.

title: A scooter turns left from the outer lane in Taiwan: what a dashcam cannot settle
summary: A scooter turns left across a car going straight at a Taiwan junction. Lane markings, earlier movement and the driver's response shape fault analysis.

title: Notarizing a Fixed-Term Lease in Taiwan: What Can Be Enforced Without a Judgment
summary: Taiwan's notarized lease deeds: conditions for enforcing fixed sums and return at term expiry, who is bound, and court challenges and stays of enforcement.

title: Crypto Traded for You in a Friend's Name: Reports and Handover Under a Taiwan Mandate
summary: If the crypto trading arrangement is a Taiwan law mandate, your friend must report its progress and hand over money received through handling that mandate.

title: Waiting for the Transfer: What a Taiwan Provisional Registration Protects
summary: A land transfer claimant needs the registered owner's written consent for caution registration. Its effect depends on the recorded claim and cancellation.

title: A Taiwan Customer in Liquidation: The Claim Notice and the Three-Month Window
summary: A Taiwan company limited by shares is liquidating. Read its creditor notice, file unpaid invoices within the announced period, and keep proof of submission.

title: Directors Abroad and a Taiwan Subsidiary's Board: Video, Proxy or a Written Vote
summary: For directors abroad, Taiwan board participation by video, another director as proxy, or a written vote depends on the meeting and each route's conditions.

title: Resigning From a Taiwan Job: Notice for an Indefinite-Term Contract
summary: An employee ending an indefinite-term contract in Taiwan must give notice based on continuous service. Longer company terms require a separate contract review.

title: Your Car, Someone Else at the Wheel: Naming the Driver on a Taiwan Traffic Notice
summary: If you believe another driver was responsible, notify the penalty authority with evidence and their documents before the appearance date; check late service.

title: Lending Spare Cash to Another Taiwan Group Company: When Article 15 of the Company Act Allows It
summary: A Taiwan company may lend funds to another if they have business dealings or need short-term financing. Item 2 caps loans at 40% of the lender's net worth.

title: One Show for Another Employer: Taiwan Work Permits, Revocation and the Three-Year Look-Back
summary: A Taiwan work permit covers work for the employer that applied for it. In a 2023 case, one ticketed show for another employer cost a US teacher a new permit.

title: Your Taiwan Account Was Used in a Scam: Can the Victim Make You Pay?
summary: A scam victim can sue the holder of a Taiwan account used in a fraud even after prosecutors declined to charge. Four rulings turned on the holder's own fault.

title: Paid a Holding Deposit in Taiwan, but the Lease Was Never Signed
summary: In Taiwan, a holding deposit paid before signing can be returned, lost or doubled. The parties' agreement and responsibility for the failed lease both matter.

title: When Is a Spouse Liable for the Other's Debts in Taiwan?
summary: Each spouse in Taiwan pays his or her own debts, but debts from family living expenses make both jointly and severally liable. Two district rulings show how.

title: A right-turning car meets a pedestrian on a Taiwan crosswalk
summary: A green light does not cancel a right-turning driver's duty to yield at a Taiwan crosswalk. A fictional scene separates the signal, contact and civil claim.

title: Appealing a Taiwan Small Claims Judgment From the United States: What the Court Will Hear, and How the 20-Day Clock Stretches
summary: A Taiwan small claims judgment can be appealed only for violating the law, within 20 days of service plus any travel-time allowance for a party abroad.

title: A Taiwan supervisor's stop notice reaches US head office
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary's statutory supervisor can require the board or a director to stop unlawful conduct, raising questions for a US parent and local directors.

title: One Defendant, Two Answers: How Taiwan Courts Decide Whether a Foreigner Under a Criminal Exit Ban May Travel Home
summary: A defendant under a criminal exit ban in Taiwan can ask the prosecutor or court to lift or change it; courts sometimes allow a few weeks home on a cash deposit.

title: Seated on a Taiwan Subsidiary's Board? How a Missed CPA Audit Turns Into Per-Person Fines
summary: If a Taiwan company needing a CPA audit approves its statements without one, each responsible person at fault, often a director, can be fined NT$10,000-50,000.

title: A US technology contract and the evidence of work contributed in Taiwan
summary: When a US supplier's service relies on a Taiwan team, work records matter to source and attribution; a contract granting technology rights needs evidence too.

title: Frozen on a Taiwan Crypto Exchange Under the Anti-Fraud Rules: The 20-Day and 48-Hour Clocks, and Why Damages Are Hard
summary: Under Taiwan's anti-fraud law an exchange can suspend an account it suspects of fraud links; police are to say within 20 days whether control continues.

title: When a Taiwan Brokerage Employee Trades Your Account: Remedies for Foreign Investors
summary: A foreign investor in a dispute with a Taiwan securities firm can seek SFIPC mediation or the Financial Ombudsman; rulings on employee trading go both ways.

title: Switching Employers Inside Taiwan on a Work Permit: The New Employer Files, and Your Start Date Follows the Permit
summary: A foreign employee switching Taiwan employers relies on the new employer's permit application, not the old employer's consent; starting early risks fines.

title: Your Child's Name in a U.S.–Taiwan Family: Taiwan's Surname Agreement, Chinese Name Rules and the CRBA
summary: A Taiwan-born child of an ROC national must be registered within 60 days, surname agreed in writing first; the CRBA uses the household record's English name.

title: Penalty Clauses in Taiwan Contracts: How Courts Cut Them Down, and When They Refuse
summary: Taiwan's Civil Code lets a court reduce an excessive contract penalty, even after partial performance; 2026 rulings show courts cutting some, refusing others.

title: A Family Member Dies in a Taiwan Hospital: Autopsy Requests, Criminal Complaints and Mandatory Mediation
summary: When a patient dies in a Taiwan hospital, a spouse or lineal relative can ask for an autopsy; since 2024 medical dispute claims must first go to mediation.

title: Visitor Activities That Can Affect Your Next Entry to Taiwan
summary: A short visit can lead to removal and a ban on returning to Taiwan. Activity evidence, basis for the ban and the deadline for challenging the decision matter.

title: Bringing a child born through surrogacy to Taiwan: parentage and a spouse’s adoption
summary: A New Taipei court approved a spouse’s adoption after surrogacy abroad, with consent and child-welfare findings. It’s one route, not a general recognition rule.

title: Approving a Taiwan Ride-Hailing Launch from US Headquarters
summary: A US headquarters assessing a Taiwan launch needs to examine current permissions. The October 22 draft and a fleet accident decision raise different questions.

title: Can someone handle my Taiwan tax after I leave? The local-agent rule in Article 72
summary: Article 72 ties a resident agent’s appointment to specific departing taxpayers, special circumstances and approval. Unpaid tax can affect departure processing.

title: A Breach at Your Taiwan Operation: Which Entity Must Report?
summary: A US company’s Taiwan incident can engage personal-data duties and reporting for designated entities. The entity, law version and evidence of care each matter.

title: A Taiwan strike reaches U.S. headquarters: damages demands, dismissals and the employee’s deadline
summary: A Taiwan subsidiary’s response to a strike may involve damages or personnel decisions. Reasons, the procedural stage and the employee’s deadline each matter.

title: Applying for Your First Taiwan ARC
summary: For your first Taiwan ARC, the filing deadline and required documents depend on how you entered and why you are staying. Application channels also vary.

title: Moving to Taiwan: Residence for Work, Study and Family
summary: Taiwan residence rules for work, study and family depend on the proposed activity, sponsor and entry visa. Eligibility needs to be settled before travel.

title: When Your Taiwan ARC Needs Updating: Renewal, Moves and Travel
summary: An ARC's expiry is only one deadline. Moving, changing jobs or losing your residence basis can trigger earlier filings; travel needs re-entry permission.

summary: 海外居住者與台灣配偶離婚前，如何整理雙方是否同意離婚、地址、外國案件、送達及出庭問題。

summary: 跨國離婚的父母如何準備子女移居諮詢：先確認由誰決定孩子住所、既有裁判與準據法，再整理生活照顧、跨境會面及扶養費。
